newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ to introduce real-time settlement by year 2000.
newsitem.headline: BOJ to introduce real-time settlement by year 2000.

text.p: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) said on Monday it planned to introduce the "real-time gross settlement system" (RTGS) for financial firms with accounts at the central bank to replace the existing settlement system by the year 2000 in an aim to reduce settlement risks.

The RTGS would allow financial institutions to settle transactions instantly on a real-time basis, whereas under the current system, transactions are settled at four specific points within a business day -- 9 a.m., 1 p.m., 3 p.m. and 5 p.m. -- through the accounts that these institutions have at the BOJ.
The current system is seen as ineffective in the event of a bank failure, as all transactions would need to be halted once any institution defaults, paralysing the entire system.
It said the biggest obstacle to the introduction of RTGS is that it would require more liquidity than the current system.
The BOJ said if a fund shortage occurred, it would provide liquidity by allowing overdrafts without interest payments.
The central bank also said financial institutions should try to tackle the problem by reducing reliance on overnight call money and doing more longer-term transactions.
The BOJ said the introduction of RTGS is in line with the efforts to bring Japan's financial markets closer to international standards.
The United States and Switzerland have already adopted the RTGS, while most European Union member countries are expected to introduce the system by the end of 1997.
